title: The Ways that Ascend to Life and the Ways that Pour into Gehenna
arc: Out of the cosmic Zone there draw forth ten paths: a chosen company that carries light upward to life through the ascending ships, and a parallel company reckoned to Error whose works in the flesh — lawlessness, killing, the wounding word against the Cross of Light, mockery of the gods — pour their travelers down into Gehenna.
reading:
This chapter sets two parallel maps of the soul's possible motion side by side. The Zone — the cosmic girdle that holds all natural states in their order — is itself crossed by paths. Out of it, the teaching says, ten ways draw forth. They are not abstract roads; they are the actual courses by which a soul, while it lives in the natural, is being carried either upward toward life or downward toward spiritual death. The number ten signals the broad completeness of these motions: every direction a human will and understanding can take is reckoned within them.

Of these ten, the teaching first separates out the chosen ways. Four of them are "reckoned to the Light": they belong to Divine Truth, and the soul that travels them is taken up "to life." Their character is ascensional — they are aligned with the light's own homeward motion, rising through the ships (the doctrinal vessels and luminaries that carry refined truth across the natural) toward the height. These are the paths along which the soul, "going forth out of them, being rescued, going within," is conveyed upward into conjunction with its source. That four are chosen corresponds to ordered fullness in extension: the four Faces of Light, the four climes through which Divine Truth manifests. The chosen paths are those four directions of life lived under influx — a complete cardinal disposition of love and wisdom that aligns the natural with the heavens.

Against this stands the other company. They too "draw forth from the Zone," they too are reckoned, but they belong to Error, the cosmic painter of false images, the wandering principle that misleads souls. Where the chosen ways go up, these "draw down to Gehenna." The teaching is explicit: Error itself shall be "removed and cast" into transmutation — its travelers undergo metensomatosis, the cycling of state through bodies as judgment after death — and three of the ways "pour forth into Gehenna." The lacunae make the exact tally hard to fix, but the structure is unmistakable: against four ways of light there stands a corresponding family of paths whose end is the tomb of unredeemed darkness.

The teaching then specifies what these descending ways actually are by naming the works through which they operate "through all flesh." The first is the abundance of lawlessness of humanity and of all flesh — the unbridled outflow of the proprium when no truth restrains it, the natural concupiscence dissolving every order. The second is the killing of every body — the murderous use of natural power, the multiplication of slaughter wherever flesh meets flesh; this is self-love expressing itself as the active extinction of the divine truth-spark in the other. The third is the wounding word — speech that strikes against the Cross of Light, against the Living Soul dispersed and crucified in matter, and against every body that bears it. So the descending paths are not merely private vices; they are assaults on the very mechanism of redemption: against the dispersed soul-light in nature, against bodies as its receptacles, and against the gods — the heavenly intelligences themselves, mocked by the cosmic Error.

Read together, the two columns make one teaching. The Zone is a crossroads. The same natural mind that can be carried upward by the four chosen paths — when its lawfulness, its love-of-life, its true word, and its honor of the heavens are aligned with influx — becomes, when it inverts each of these into lawlessness, killing, wounding speech, and mockery, the very vehicle by which Error draws souls down into Gehenna. The eight (or however many the missing text named) descending ways are precisely the inverted images of the ascending ones: each work of light has its counter-work in the flesh. The Cross of Light is the hinge. To honor the dispersed soul-light in every body is to walk the chosen way; to wound it in flesh by lawlessness, killing, and blasphemous word is to walk Error's way down. The teaching's whole movement is therefore a sober map for self-examination: every path the soul is on right now is one of these ten, and only the four that ascend with the light arrive at life.
